qs.q: Is multi-factor sign-in turned on for email and admin accounts?
qs.fix: Turn on multi-factor sign-in for email and every admin account first.

qs.q: Does everyone use a password manager for work logins?
qs.fix: Roll out a password manager and retire reused passwords.

qs.q: Do leavers lose access within one working day?
qs.fix: Write a leaver checklist and revoke accounts the day someone departs.

qs.q: Are admin rights limited to the people who need them?
qs.fix: List admin accounts and remove rights nobody needs.

qs.q: Are shared accounts avoided or tracked?
qs.fix: Replace shared logins with named accounts, or record who holds each one.

qs.q: Are laptops and phones encrypted?
qs.fix: Enable built-in disk encryption on every laptop and phone.

qs.q: Are critical patches applied within 14 days?
qs.fix: Set a 14-day target for critical patches and track it monthly.

qs.q: Do you keep a list of company devices and software?
qs.fix: Start a simple inventory sheet of devices and key software.

qs.q: Is endpoint protection running on every computer?
qs.fix: Install and centrally monitor endpoint protection on all computers.

qs.q: Are automatic updates and screen locks switched on?
qs.fix: Enforce automatic updates and a short screen-lock timeout.

qs.q: Is your critical data backed up automatically?
qs.fix: Automate backups of the data you could not afford to lose.

qs.q: Is a copy kept offsite or offline?
qs.fix: Keep one backup copy offsite or offline.

qs.q: Have you restored from a backup in the last year?
qs.fix: Test a restore this quarter and write down how long it took.

qs.q: Is there a written target for how fast you must recover?
qs.fix: Agree a recovery time target for each critical system.

qs.q: Are backups protected if an account is compromised?
qs.fix: Use separate credentials and delete protection for backups.

name: Email and people
soc: Security: control environment and communication (CC1, CC2)

qs.q: Has everyone had phishing awareness training?
qs.fix: Run a short phishing session for all staff each year.

qs.q: Are SPF, DKIM and DMARC set up for your domain?
qs.fix: Publish SPF, DKIM and DMARC records for your email domain.

qs.q: Is there an easy way to report a suspicious email?
qs.fix: Add a report button or a single address for suspicious emails.

qs.q: Does everyone know who to tell if something goes wrong?
qs.fix: Name an incident contact and share it with the whole team.

qs.q: Do new starters get security basics on day one?
qs.fix: Add a short security briefing to onboarding.

name: Governance and SOC 2 readiness
soc: Security: risk assessment and vendor risk (CC3, CC9)

qs.q: Is there a written security policy approved by leadership?
qs.fix: Write a short security policy and have leadership approve it.

qs.q: Do you keep a risk register and review it yearly?
qs.fix: Start a risk register with your top ten risks and review it yearly.

qs.q: Are suppliers with access to your data reviewed first?
qs.fix: Review security basics for any supplier that handles your data.

qs.q: Do you have a written incident response plan?
qs.fix: Write a one-page incident plan: who, what, and who to call.

qs.q: Are access and security logs kept and reviewed?
qs.fix: Keep logs for at least 90 days and review them on a schedule.
